Q: Is there anything bad about having multiple imports on one line? A:

This is an example of a PEP formatting rule that does not take into account small screens or vision disabilities. It should be perfectly acceptable to list multiple, similar-type packages on the same line like:

import datetime, time
import sys, os, glob

"Readability", as stated in PEP, is for people who do not need to increase the font size to see things clearly. Also, PEP ignores the fact that 95% of all screens have more horizontal space than vertical space. The guidelines should strive to use as much of the horizontal space as possible so that the programmer can to see as many lines of code on a single screen.

Q: What is Base94 encoding and how does it work? A:

Essentially: Base94 encoding takes 9 input bytes of 8 bits each, uses those to construct a 72-bit integer, and then converts that to an 11-digit base-94 number, and encodes that number using the ASCII characters ! (33) through ~ (126):

!"#$%&'()*+,-./0123456789:;<=>?@ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ[\]^_`abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz{|}~
